author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian list by specialty on both the page and the machine-readable surface
summary: Both veterinarian-list surfaces accept an optional specialty filter carried in the URL. A named specialty narrows the listing to veterinarians holding it; the HTML page pages within the narrowed list, the machine-readable list returns only matching veterinarians. Delivers REQ-VET-003 (page) and REQ-VET-004 (reinstated machine-readable surface).
acceptance_criteria: The HTML directory with a named specialty in its address lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, a page at a time, with paging staying within the narrowed list
The specialty filter matches the whole specialty name and ignores letter case on both surfaces; a value that is only part of a specialty name matches nothing
An empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as though no filter were named on both surfaces; with no filter, each surface behaves exactly as it does today
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields an ordinary successful result with an empty veterinarian list (HTTP 200) on both surfaces, not a failure
The machine-readable veterinarian list is served as a supported surface and, with a named specialty, returns only veterinarians holding it
The HTML directory's pagination links carry the named specialty so a narrowed listing stays navigable across pages
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search (NG-9 keeps this out)
Any on-page control for the filter — form, dropdown, or menu; the filter is a URL contract only in this scope, and a visible control may come as a follow-up request
notes: One vertical slice through the vet feature package (controller, repository, page template) delivering both REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004; the machine-readable surface is reinstated under REQ-VET-004 while the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. Open question recorded in PRD: whether surrounding whitespace on a non-empty specialty value should be trimmed to mirror owner search; narrowest reading taken for this slice is no trimming, so ' surgery ' matches nothing. Product owner has stated no further product answers will come.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Additive optional specialty filter on the two existing vet-list surfaces. No new module, pattern, dependency, or bounded context. It follows the codebase's declarative-repository + controller-request-param idiom: the owner last-name filter (OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith driven from OwnerController.processFindForm) is the direct precedent. The product-level NG-9 tension is already settled by the accepted non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md, which narrows NG-9 to admit specialty filtering and reinstates /vets as a supported surface under REQ-VET-004 — so this is not conflicting. The one durable-memory correction (the Known Defects row that called /vets 'pending removal', now false) plus the Implements wiring for VetController/VetRepository/Vets have been applied to docs/system-design.md.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a specialty-filter query used by both surfaces; the existing @Cacheable('vets') stays on the two findAll methods only
VetController branches on presence of the specialty param: absent/blank keeps today's findAll paths, present calls the filter query
vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty param — the owner template does NOT carry its filter across pages, so this is a small net-new bit, not copyable from owners
controller adds 'specialty' to the model so the template can append it to pagination hrefs

patterns.description: declarative paged derived-query filter (findByLastNameStartingWith) — the placement precedent: put the matching rule in a Spring Data derived-query method, not hand-rolled SQL
controller branch on a blank filter value (empty string signifies broadest search); mirror the blank-vs-present branch, but see the trimming risk below

risks.risk: Trimming semantics: OwnerController strips the value; the PRD's narrowest reading forbids trimming the vet match value, so ' surgery ' must match nothing. Copying the owner strip() would violate REQ-VET-003.
risks.mitigation: Detect blank with a hasText/isBlank check (whitespace-only => treat as absent, per criterion) but pass the RAW untrimmed value to the matcher. Blank-detection and value-trimming are distinct — do the first, not the second.

risks.risk: Whole-name vs prefix and case: a partial specialty value must match nothing; matching is case-insensitive.
risks.mitigation: Use equality + IgnoreCase, NOT StartingWith. Recommended repo method findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) for the page and a Collection-returning overload for the JSON surface; 'Distinct' guards against duplicate Vet rows from the vet_specialties ManyToMany join. Both derive from the same property path + IgnoreCase, so matching is identical across surfaces by construction (satisfies the 'identical on both surfaces' criterion).

risks.risk: Caching: the new filter methods should not reuse the 'vets' cache blindly.
risks.mitigation: Leave the filter query methods uncached — dataset is tiny and filtering is not hot. Do not fold a new cache key into this slice.

risks.risk: No-match page must be HTTP 200 with empty list; empty-filtered pagination.
risks.mitigation: With a repo-derived Page the empty result yields totalPages 0 and the template's th:if=totalPages>1 block simply does not render — no special handling needed. Prefer the repo-derived Page over manual in-memory sublist paging to avoid page-out-of-range handling.

notes: Verdict minor: existing pattern with small adjustments; small system-design.md updates applied (removed the stale 'machine-readable route pending removal' Known Defects row; wired REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004 into the VetController/VetRepository/Vets Implements cells and their purpose text). No ADR authored — the load-bearing product decision already lives in docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md and the tactical repo-vs-controller choice is not ADR-worthy. Alternative acceptable placement: filter in-memory over cached findAll() with a single predicate s.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(specialty) and manual paging — reuses the cache and keeps one shared matcher, but requires manual pagination; the repo-derived query is the more idiomatic recommendation here. No autofix records to audit. IDE oracle not consulted for the resolution claims — the covering precedent (findByLastNameStartingWith) was confirmed by Read of OwnerRepository/OwnerController; the load-bearing template/pagination evidence is HTML the Java oracle cannot see.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Specialty filter uses a Spring Data derived query (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) with bound parameters — no SQL/JPQL injection surface introduced
Thymeleaf link expression @{/vets.html(...,specialty=${specialty})} URL-encodes the parameter and HTML-escapes the attribute, so the echoed specialty cannot break out for reflected XSS
Raw untrimmed specialty value crosses no unsafe boundary: it is only a JPA bind parameter and an URL-encoded query param
/vets JSON surface exposes only vet names and specialty names — no new PII or secret exposure
Blank/whitespace filter handled via StringUtils.hasText, preserving today's unfiltered behavior with no fail-open path

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: VetRepository: two new derived-query methods use IgnoreCase (whole-name equality, not StartingWith prefix) and Distinct to collapse duplicate rows from the vet_specialties ManyToMany join — correct by construction
VetRepository: new filter methods carry no @Cacheable annotation — correctly left uncached per design, with the rationale explained in the Javadoc
VetRepository: both new methods are fully documented (matching semantics, Distinct rationale, caching decision) — the Javadoc is load-bearing context for future readers

VetController: StringUtils.hasText used for blank detection on both surfaces — correctly distinguishes blank-detection from value-trimming; raw untrimmed value passed to the repository so whitespace-only specialty matches nothing

VetController: specialty added to the model only when hasText is true — when absent/blank the model attribute is null, and Thymeleaf's @{} URL expression silently drops null parameters, so pagination links omit specialty correctly on unfiltered listings
VetController: findPaginated branches on hasText and delegates to the filter query or findAll accordingly — no controller-side in-memory trimming of the result set

vetList.html: all five pagination link types (numbered, first, prev, next, last) carry specialty=${specialty} — when the model attribute is null Thymeleaf suppresses the parameter, keeping unfiltered pagination clean; when present the narrowed listing stays navigable across pages
Constructor injection with package-private class — consistent with the existing codebase pattern

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Four new tests added to ClinicServiceTests use the pre-2026-07-31 `should*` naming convention instead of the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` BDD school required by testing-principles.md for tests written after 2026-07-31. The methods are: `shouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialtyByWholeNameIgnoringCase`, `shouldNotMatchASpecialtyByPartialName`, `shouldReturnNoVetsForAnUnheldSpecialty`, `shouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialtyAsACollectionIgnoringCase`. Rename to e.g. `theVetRepositoryShouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialtyByWholeNameIgnoringCase`, `theVetRepositoryShouldNotMatchASpecialtyByPartialName`, `theVetRepositoryShouldReturnNoVetsForAnUnheldSpecialty`, `theVetRepositoryShouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialtyAsACollectionIgnoringCase`.
findings.fix: Rename the four new test methods to follow the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` convention per testing-principles.md § Test Naming.

findings.description: The non-trimming semantic is not tested. The design-block explicitly flagged it as a risk: a non-blank but whitespace-padded value such as `' surgery '` must match nothing (because no trimming is applied per the narrowest PRD reading), and this is distinct from the blank/whitespace-only case that `theVetPageShouldIgnoreABlankSpecialty` covers. Without a test for the padded-but-non-empty case, a future refactor that accidentally trims the value would pass all current tests. Add tests `theVetPageShouldTreatAPaddedSpecialtyAsALiteralValue` and `theVetsResourceShouldTreatAPaddedSpecialtyAsALiteralValue` (or equivalent names) that supply `' surgery '` and assert an empty result list on both surfaces.
